title: Gabriel de Gramont, bishop of Tarbes, Rome, to Montmorency, 11 Oct 1529, BnF fr. 3091 no. 23 ff. 45r-47v (catalogue item 6, Gramont's cipher 1529)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the leaves or in print found (Wirtz-Daviau's edition of Chabot's embassy not checked). Lasry decoded the text in 2023, unpublished.

transcription.source: Gallica full-resolution canvases 49-52, line crops; glyph aliases in aliases/f45r.txt-f47v.txt
transcription.notes: Count measured with _check_profile.py --measure --letters on the six alias files concatenated (f46r's L01| line labels stripped): 4002 signs, 37 distinct. Flagged measured false only because no single file holds it. The site's 'about 7,000 signs' is not a measured figure.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on graphic signs ('Gramont's cipher (1529)', Lasry's table; siblings fr. 3040 f. 16 and Clair. 330 f. 53), several homophones for common letters, doubled-letter and COM/CON signs, a few nulls and code signs for persons.
system.sibling_key: Lasry's 2023 table 'Gramont's cipher (1529)' on cryptiana GL.htm, built from fr. 3040 f. 16 and Clair. 330 f. 53; applied unchanged.
system.notes: Distinct count measured on the six alias files concatenated (aliases/f45r-f47v.txt); it includes the alias characters for nulls and separators. Code signs identified here from context: heart = roy; three unlisted large signs stand for the Emperor, the Florentines and the Pope/Medici. '#' is A as often as M; the ♀-on-foot sign is a null.

prior_solution.where: Key published online by Lasry (table dated 5 Nov 2023 on Tomokiyo's cryptiana GL.htm). Lasry also decoded this letter in 2023, with the other three of catalogue item 6, but never published the decipherment (Lasry, 21 Sept 2026). 'partial': key public, reading unpublished.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code and posed the catalogue item; no target-specific intervention recorded. Relayed Lasry's 21 Sept 2026 correction on his unpublished decipherments.
tools: Gallica image scripts (thumbs.py, full.py, crop.py, sheet.py)

solution.what: Matched the four items against Tomokiyo's francis.htm and GL.htm: four letters, four different keys, all tabulated by Lasry in 2023; no plaintext on either site.
Located the correct Gallica arks (fr. 3091 is btv1b9060253s, not the catalogue's) and fetched full-resolution canvases.
Transcribed the 171 cipher lines of ff. 45r-47v at glyph level into ASCII aliases, page by page, by parallel per-page agents (aliases/f45r.txt-f47v.txt, f45r_transcription.md-f47v_transcription.md).
Applied Lasry's 'Gramont's cipher (1529)' table with decode.py; first full line decodes to 'tredecime v & avltre v'.
Read the letter in full (each page 90-95 % secure); heart = the King, three unlisted person signs inferred from context, a null sign identified.
Dated to 1529 by Clement VII's departure from Rome for Bologna, the bull of the four décimes and Orange before Florence.

Correction from George Lasry: he decoded all four texts in 2023 when reconstructing the keys, but the decipherments were never published. Prior-solution record updated: a reading existed, unpublished, learned of after the reading and not used (only his keys were).

Split the combined catalogue item 6 entry under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): four letters in four keys. gramont1529 keeps fr. 3091 no. 23 (Gramont's cipher 1529); langeac1529 takes fr. 3083 no. 8 (Avranches' cipher 1); gramont1530 takes fr. 3071 no. 7 (Gramont's cipher 1530); the Mâcon letter fr. 3071 no. 4 moved to rome1536 with the other letters in Mascon's cipher.

outcome.method_basis: Read with Lasry's 2023 table 'Gramont's cipher (1529)' for this letter (cryptiana GL.htm), applied unchanged to a new glyph transcription; no new cryptanalysis.
outcome.fraction_read_source: aliases/f45r.txt-f47v.txt concatenated: 4,002 signs, 12 of them '?' (unidentified); every other sign has a value and every line gives French. The transcribers graded each page 90-95 % secure; doubtful phrases are listed in NOTES.
outcome.notes: Read in full; doubtful: single letters per page, 'fier ni a nui' (f. 45r), 'en voi[e]' (f. 45v), first word of f. 47v l. 7; four code-sign identities inferred from context.
